items.claim: Ezek.8.1-8.6 holds one movement. The dated frame opens it: Ezek.8.1 carries a year-bearing date together with the hand idiom in its divine-name-pair form, Ezek.8.3 carries the lifting by the Spirit and the in-visions-of-God frame, and Ezek.8.4 the glory notice; the first tableau then runs Ezek.8.5-8.6 and ends on the again-see pointer at Ezek.8.6. The hand idiom stands at seven verses book-wide (Ezek.1.3, 3.14, 3.22, 8.1, 33.22, 37.1, 40.1) and Ezek.8.1 is the one of those seven reading the divine-name pair, so the exclusivity statement holds on the bytes. medium_low matches the evidence, because the close is a pointer that looks forward rather than a refrain.
items.both_sides: Onset side: Ezek.7.27 ends the preceding unit on the recognition refrain and the mark layer puts a pe on that verse, while Ezek.8.1 stacks a date and the hand idiom, with a transport following at Ezek.8.3. Close side: Ezek.8.6 carries the again-see pointer (sweep: 3 verses, Ezek.8.6, 8.13, 8.15), and MT 8:6 also carries a samekh. Because the pointer reaches ahead to the tableau at Ezek.8.7-8.13, it links across the seam as well as closing this unit, which is why a hold below high is right here.

items.claim: Two different devices are merged into one census in this row's rejected-alternative prose. The again-see pointer stands at three verses (Ezek.8.6, 8.13, 8.15); the have-you-seen question stands at four (Ezek.8.12, 8.15, 8.17, 47.6). Ezek.8.17 carries the question and not the pointer, so the four-verse pointer run named there (Ezek.8.6, 8.13, 8.15, 8.17) blends the two counts. The span Ezek.8.7-8.13 is itself one tableau and stands: a transport opens it at Ezek.8.7 and the pointer closes it at Ezek.8.13.
items.both_sides: Onset side: Ezek.8.7 carries the he-brought-me transport form, which stands at four verses book-wide (Ezek.8.7, 8.14, 8.16, 40.1), and the mark layer puts a samekh on MT 8:6 behind it. Close side: Ezek.8.13 is a bare speech carrying the pointer alone, and Ezek.8.14 opens the next tableau on the same transport form. On the flagged absence claim: the ch-8 marks stand on MT 8:6 and MT 8:14 only, and the single ch-8 ketiv/qere site is MT 8:6, so nothing inside Ezek.8.7-8.13 is left undisclosed; the flagged mark is the one behind the onset, cited in the row by its verse.

items.claim: Ezek.8.14-8.18 holds two transport-opened tableaux, not one. The Tammuz scene opens on the transport at Ezek.8.14 and closes at Ezek.8.15 on the again-see pointer, the same close the units ending at Ezek.8.6 and Ezek.8.13 use; the sun-worship scene then opens at Ezek.8.16 on the identical he-brought-me form (sweep: 4 verses, Ezek.8.7, 8.14, 8.16, 40.1), moves to a new place with new participants, and closes on the wrath declaration at Ezek.8.18. A seam therefore falls at Ezek.8.15/8.16 on the same onset and close devices that draw the seams at Ezek.8.7 and Ezek.8.14.
items.both_sides: Close side of the proposed seam: Ezek.8.15 pairs the have-you-seen question with the again-see pointer, the device that ends the two tableaux before it, and nothing in Ezek.8.15 reaches forward into the sun-worship scene. Onset side: Ezek.8.16 carries the same transport form as this row's own onset verse and introduces the inner court, the twenty-five men and the eastward posture that the wrath declaration at Ezek.8.18 answers. Mark evidence: the ch-8 marks stand on MT 8:6 and MT 8:14 only, so neither side of Ezek.8.15/8.16 carries one and neither side is weakened by that; the samekh on MT 8:14 falls one verse inside this row and is disclosed there.

suggested_fix.fact: Ezek.8.16 opens the sun-worship tableau on the he-brought-me transport form (sweep: 4 verses, Ezek.8.7, 8.14, 8.16, 40.1) and Ezek.8.15 closes the Tammuz tableau on the again-see pointer (sweep: 3 verses, Ezek.8.6, 8.13, 8.15); Ezek.8.16-8.18 is three verses

items.claim: A byte-true device straddles this row's onset seam and is not disclosed: the run for crying in the prophet's ears with a loud voice stands at exactly two verses, Ezek.8.18 and Ezek.9.1 (consonantal-skeleton identity; the accents differ), so the unheard human cry that ends the temple tour is answered by the divine cry that opens this unit. The seam itself holds: Ezek.9.1 summons a new participant set, the scene runs to a narrative task report at Ezek.9.11, and MT 9:11 carries a samekh.
items.both_sides: Onset side: Ezek.9.1 opens on the cry-phrase, now a summons of the city's executioners, with no competing formula. Close side of the unit before it: Ezek.8.18 ends the tour with the wrath declaration whose last clause carries the same phrase. The repetition binds the two verses across the seam while place, actors and action all change at Ezek.9.1, so the seam stands and the link is owed a disclosure rather than a re-drawing. Inside the row, the samekh on MT 9:3 falls between the glory's rise and the marking command, which the row weighs and does not adopt; the calling clause at Ezek.9.3 and the command at Ezek.9.4 are one speech act, so the mark is rightly not taken.

items.claim: Ezek.10.1-10.8 is one movement: the sight of the sapphire throne at Ezek.10.1, the coal command at Ezek.10.2, the glory rising from the cherub to the threshold at Ezek.10.4 (the glory phrase stands at nine verses book-wide), and the errand carried out and completed at Ezek.10.6-10.7. The closing verse belongs with it, because the man-hand notice at Ezek.10.8 accounts for the cherub hand that Ezek.10.7 has just stretched out to deliver the fire, tying the two verses by the same term.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 9:11 carries a samekh and the preceding scene ends there on a completed task report, while Ezek.10.1 opens on the sight-formula. Close side: Ezek.10.7 ends with the linen-clad man taking the fire and going out, Ezek.10.8 accounts for the hand that gave it to him, and Ezek.10.9 restarts with the same sight-formula for the wheels. On the flagged absence claim: the mark layer records no parashah mark anywhere in ch 10, the marks running from MT 9:11 to MT 11:1, so the chapter-wide statement holds; the flagged mark is the one standing behind this unit's onset, cited in the row by its verse.

items.claim: The stated ground for holding this row at low is not what the bytes carry. Ezek.10.9 opens on the same sight-formula that opens Ezek.10.1, and as an opener that formula stands at four verses book-wide (Ezek.2.9, 8.2, 10.1, 10.9). The onset therefore rests on the device class already accepted as the opener at Ezek.10.1, and the span Ezek.10.9-10.17 stands as drawn.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the sight-formula at Ezek.10.9 introduces the four wheels in the same construction that introduces the throne at Ezek.10.1, and what follows is sustained description. Close side: Ezek.10.17 ends that description on the summary clause about the spirit of the living creature, and Ezek.10.18 restarts narrated action with the glory leaving the threshold. Neither side carries a parashah mark, since ch 10 carries none, so the seam rests on the sight-formula at the onset and the description-to-narration turn at the close, which is the same weight of evidence the unit at Ezek.10.1-10.8 is held at.

Close side: Ezek.10.22 completes the identification begun at Ezek.10.15 and Ezek.10.20, and Ezek.11.1 opens the next unit on the lifting of the prophet by the Spirit with a new participant set at the east gate. Mark evidence weighed and not taken as decisive: ch 10 carries no parashah mark and the next one is the pe on MT 11:1, so the tradition's section runs one verse past this seam; a text signal drives where a mark informs, and the transport at Ezek.11.1 is the text signal here.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether Ezek.10.8 closes the coal errand or opens the cherub description. Its notice of a man-shaped hand under the wings recurs at Ezek.10.21, and the under-their-wings phrase stands at three verses (Ezek.1.8, 10.8, 10.21), which would group Ezek.10.8 with the description; against that, Ezek.10.7 names the cherub's own outstretched hand, which Ezek.10.8 accounts for.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It moves one verse between two adjacent units in the one chapter of this span carrying no parashah mark at all, so no mark evidence can settle it either way.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether Ezek.10.15 belongs inside a unit characterised as static description: it narrates the cherubim mounting up, the action Ezek.10.18-10.19 completes, while the verses on either side of it describe.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If Ezek.10.15 is narration, the description proper is Ezek.10.9-10.14 and the ascent runs from Ezek.10.15, which would redraw both seams inside Ezek.10.9-10.22 rather than one.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the samekh on MT 8:14 argues a seam between the Tammuz sighting and the speech at Ezek.8.15 rather than after Ezek.8.15. The tradition's ch-8 division, after MT 8:6 and after MT 8:14, sits one verse out of phase with the again-see pointer at Ezek.8.6, 8.13 and 8.15, and the inventory does not carry where inside a verse a mark falls.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The cut proposed at Ezek.8.16 rests on the pointer and the transport; a mark-led division would instead cut after Ezek.8.14, which would leave the pointer verse opening a unit rather than closing one and would contradict the closes already drawn at Ezek.8.6 and Ezek.8.13.
